Subject: Throughput & Canary Sizing — alignment after discovery

Alex / Jordan — thanks again for the time earlier today. Short note to capture what we heard, the constraints that matter for sizing, and a tight set of next steps so we can scope a PoC that proves both latency and cost targets.

What we heard (pain points)
- Tail latency spikes during morning and evening peaks causing timeouts in the inference tier (currently 300–500ms P95).
- Cost volatility from over-provisioning when traffic bursts occur; unclear how to size GPU pools for mixed short/long prompts.
- Long-chat sessions create KV-cache pressure which increases per-request latency and memory contention.

Customer goals / acceptance criteria
- Steady-state latency target: P95 <= 120ms for prompts <= 256 tokens.
- Burst capacity: handle short bursts up to ~1.2k QPS for 60s without dropping requests (degraded quality acceptable to maintain availability).
- Throughput profile: expected baseline 350 QPS (median prompt 90 tokens), with bursts to 1.2k QPS (median prompt 40 tokens).
- Quality: primary model equivalent to open 13B-class (high-quality quantized) with a 70B-quality fallback for regressions.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is required; retention window ~90 days.

Technical constraints we discussed
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated pool in us-west1 (customer-sited tenancy) with a canary pool for validation.
- KV cache: session-affinity recommended for chat flows longer than 10 messages; prefix caching for common system prompts.
- Autoscaling: combination of request-based and queue-depth scaling vs. strict CPU/GPU utilization thresholds.

Proposed approach (PoC scope)
1) Canary baseline: 10% traffic to 1x small dedicated pool (2x A100-80GB equiv) for 24 hours; automated rollback if P95 latency > 140ms or error rate increases >1.5x.
2) Rapid scale test: synthetic bursts to 1.2k QPS for 1 minute to validate burst autoscaling and pre-warm behavior.
3) KV cache evaluation: run long-session replay (50 sessions, 10–20 messages each) to observe KV eviction and tail latency.
4) Cost estimate: capacity model + per-token cost estimate (we'll produce after we get sample traffic distributions / token histogram).

Attachments: MVP test plan attached (mvp_test_plan.pdf) — includes synthetic test scripts and success criteria.

Immediate next steps (action owner)
- Alex: share a 48-hour traffic sample (CSV or GCP load logs) and a small set of representative prompts (link to Drive is fine). — due Tue 2027-05-04
- Karthik: produce a capacity sketch (GPU count, expected batching, quantization options) and a canary runbook. — first draft Mon 2027-05-03
- Hannah/Grace: schedule a technical deep-dive to lock in model variants and rollout thresholds (propose Wed 2027-05-05 10:00 PDT).

If this aligns, we'll prepare the mutual action plan and an initial cost envelope for the PoC.

Thanks — Hannah

Thanks — quick technical notes that will feed into the capacity sketch:

Batching & latency
- Target batching window: 6–8 ms for steady-state to keep P95 in budget while preserving throughput. For short prompts (<=128 tokens) we can push to smaller windows to reduce latency.
- Continuous batching on the serving runtime + request-based dynamic batch sizing will give the best tradeoffs.

GPU footprints & quantization
- For the 13B-class quantized path: 2x A100-80GB equivalents should handle ~250–300 QPS at median 90 tokens with 8~12ms avg token latency (depends on prompt).
- Plan on a 3–4 node dedicated pool for baseline (allows room for maintenance and one-pop surge handling) — we'll provide exact vGPU/core counts in the sketch.
- Recommend int8 quantization (AWQ/LLM.int8 equivalent) for the 13B path; expect ~1–3% quality delta vs float16 on most tasks.

Canary & fallbacks
- Canary: 10% for 24h -> 50% for 48h with rollback triggers: P95 latency > 140ms, error rate + latency slope, or quality regression on a small eval set.
- Fallback policy: if canary fails, route traffic to the 70B variant in a different pool (higher cost) to preserve quality while ops investigate.

KV cache behavior
- For long chats we recommend sticky routing to keep KV locality; eviction observed when average session context > 12k tokens. We'll instrument per-session KV hit rates during the PoC.

I'll have the first capacity sketch and a rough cost envelope by EOD Mon 2027-05-03.

-Karthik
